question.problem:
Consider the vector subspace $H=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -11\end{aligned}]\}.$ Which of the following vectors belong to ${H}^{⊥}?$

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -14 \\ -6\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 14 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors that span the subspace $H$ as ${h}_{1}$ and ${h}_{2}.$ 

Now, a vector $v$ belongs to ${H}^{⊥}$ if $v$ is orthogonal to the set of vectors that spans the subspace $H.$ So, we have to find the products ${v}_{i}\cdot {h}_{j}$ for $i=1,2,3$ and  $j=1,2.$  

- For ${v}_{1}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {h}_{1} & =5\cdot (-6)+(-2)\cdot 0+6\cdot 5=0 & ✓ \\ {v}_{1}\cdot {h}_{2} & =5\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 4+6\cdot (-11)=-64\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, ${v}_{1}\notin {H}^{⊥}.$

- For ${v}_{2}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2}\cdot {h}_{1} & =5\cdot (-6)+(-14)\cdot 0+(-6)\cdot 5=-60\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, ${v}_{2}\notin {H}^{⊥}.$ We do not need to test ${v}_{2}\cdot {h}_{2}.$

- For ${v}_{3}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\cdot {h}_{1} & =5\cdot (-6)+14\cdot 0+6\cdot 5=0 & ✓ \\ {v}_{3}\cdot {h}_{2} & =5\cdot 2+14\cdot 4+6\cdot (-11)=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, ${v}_{3}\in {H}^{⊥}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${v}_{3}$ only".
